# CLI v5 Templates - Fabio-first object-model proposal

**PROPOSED — NOT APPROVED FOR IMPLEMENTATION**

**Date:** October 31, 2026  
**Candidate:** `feature/templates-engine-redesign` at `c8559f8e1f0ba0bd3e1fed39e68934c836f5b32b` (tree `3243a0529b2505f39e76ba2b0543545ff77b905c`).  
**Scope:** Design only. No product implementation, runtime validation, or GA acceptance is claimed.

## 1. Executive summary

Extend the retained `Templater` from **listing installed templates** to **resolving one eligible family and invoking one exact, session-bound variant**. Keep the existing factory, context, catalog entry, parameter projection, and Microsoft.TemplateEngine session. Add only the resolution/invocation values needed by the commands. `func init` and `func new` own user input, prompts, stack-specific interpretation, guarded publication, and required CLI finalization. Neither command can use this contract end to end today.

First prove one item template through `func new`, then one project template through `func init`, without removing working stack initializers. Two proof templates are not the release inventory: Fabio's draft proposes minimal project and item coverage across supported stacks, while the actual GA matrix and historical negative item cases need team decisions and qualification.

## 4. Minimal recommended object model

| Fabio concept | Recommendation, owner and lifetime |
|---|---|
| `ITemplaterFactory` | **Keep existing interface.** DI-owned; `Create(context)` synchronously supplies a caller-owned `Templater`. No second factory. |
| `TemplateEngineContext` | **Keep existing record.** CLI captures resolved directory, optional project root/stack/language and resolved bundle once per command. Do not embed mutable parser, console, or the whole `FunctionsProject`. Add a field only if an actual template requires it. |
| `Templater` | **Extend existing session owner.** Reuse `ListAsync(TemplateType)` and package manager; add scoped family resolution from a user reference or an entry *issued by this session*. Reuse one snapshot/engine environment through resolution and invocation. Dispose on every exit. |
| `TemplateCatalogEntry` | **Keep one concrete installed-variant descriptor.** It describes even unavailable entries; freeze its alias/parameter collections for the command. Never invoke solely by display name or fabricate an available candidate when metadata/package details are unusable. Session-private mapping binds an issued entry to its actual engine template/source, not another public catalog. |
| `TemplateGroup` | **Keep as a small immutable resolved-family view**, not a service or graph: explicit family identity, eligible `ResolvedTemplate` members, and exclusion diagnostics. With no declared group, propose a singleton keyed by scoped exact identity. `Narrow` applies only first-journey selection fields and returns a new view; zero members retain reasons. Confirm fallback and precedence with real metadata. |
| `ResolvedTemplate` | **Add a restricted, session-bound exact-variant handle.** It exposes its existing descriptor/parameter definitions and invokes through the originating `Templater`. Reject foreign/stale entries and invocation after disposal; no name-based re-resolution. |
| `TemplateParameterDefinition` | **Keep existing canonical projection.** `TemplateParameterProjector` already handles aliases, types, choices, requiredness, defaults, and visibility, excluding the command-owned `name` symbol. Carry explicit/default/project-derived value provenance in binding for the invocation, not a duplicate mutable parameter schema. |
| `TemplateInvocationRequest` | **Add one small value for the selected handle:** intended destination, canonical parameter values, and only the required collision intent. No template identity, engine selector, raw tokens, or prompt callbacks. Invocation validates values and destination syntax before private rendering; CLI rechecks actual destination state before publication. |
| `TemplateInvocationResult` | **Add a typed render outcome:** diagnostics and planned file/directory output (plus minimal finalization inputs), with bounded ownership of any private output. Planned effects are **not actual writes or command success**; the CLI separately reports publication/configuration effects. No generic package action list. |

Small internal resolution status/diagnostic/criteria values are justified only to distinguish not found, wrong kind, ambiguous family, zero eligible variants, invalid input, and invocation failure. Keep the C# surface internal unless a demonstrated assembly boundary needs visibility. `TemplateType` already corresponds to the draft's proposed `TemplateKind`; no parallel enum.

## 5. `func new` and `func init` flows

These are **proposed** handoffs. A named component here is not evidence that the implementation already exists.

### `func new` - item journey

| Transition / owner | Input -> output and reused seam | Gate, missing work, failure |
|---|---|---|
| Entry / `Program` | Parsed command -> handler, or first-run setup and rerun notice (`Program.cs:99-109`). | Successful interactive first-run setup returns 0 before `NewCommand`; do not promise its migration exit code on every invocation. Cancellation has its own nonzero path. |
| Parse / CLI | `[path]`, `--template`, `--name`, `--force`, `--non-interactive`, `--list`, `--format` -> target and raw template inputs (`NewCommand.cs:15-59`, `PathArgument.cs`). | `System.CommandLine` currently knows only built-ins: design a **bounded command-specific way to retain template tokens before unknown-option parse errors prevent invocation**. Reject unknown/duplicate explicit inputs after candidate binding; do not silently add `--output` or package-coordinate flags. |
| Project / CLI + Stack | Target -> `IFunctionsProjectResolver` result, effective stack/language, relevant bundle/workload evidence. | Use the target, not an unrelated cwd; distinguish unsupported item workload from missing project. The current handler still creates nothing. |
| Session and list / CLI + `Templater` | Captured `TemplateEngineContext` -> installed item entries in the shared hive. | `--list` may show valid visible entries and actionable unavailable/incompatible diagnostics without applying creation-only gates. Hide ordinary hidden entries; explicit hidden-ID policy remains open. Missing/corrupt content is not successful empty discovery. |
| Resolve/select / `Templater` + CLI | Scoped ID or declared alias -> exactly one family; narrowed eligible variants -> exact handle. | Identity before aliases; do not infer family from display text. A lone variant in an **explicitly selected** family can be used; absent choice or ambiguity fails non-interactively. Interactive prompting/policy for multiple variants stays with CLI; no incidental list-order precedence. |
| Bind/validate / CLI + Stack + handle | Selected descriptor and project inputs -> canonical values and required-value diagnostics. | Parse candidate-specific tokens against that descriptor; map built-ins deliberately, prompt only missing required values, reject invalid explicit ones. Reuse projector; do not interpret .NET/Python project files inside shared engine. |
| Render/compose / `ResolvedTemplate` + Stack | Validated request -> private planned file/directory effects and Stack integration inputs. | Engine invocation and output capture do not exist yet. For future .NET/Python items, stack-owned project edits or append composition need concrete qualified contracts; no direct target generation, hidden package install, or arbitrary post-actions. |
| Preflight/publish / CLI | Planned effects and originals -> checked collision/force permission, then actual effect record. | Verify paths, protected ancestry and originals before mutation; create without force refuses existing target, force permits only guarded replacement. Failure before publication leaves target unchanged; after mutation report completed and uncertain effects. |
| Finalize/dispose / CLI | Published files -> supported Stack follow-up (if required), diagnostic/exit status; dispose session. | `func new` does **not** create init configuration. Required follow-up failure is not success; distinguish cancellation/partial effects and dispose even on list, rejection or render failure. |

### `func init` - project journey

| Transition / owner | Input -> output and reused seam | Gate, missing work, failure |
|---|---|---|
| Entry/parse / `Program`, `InitCommand` | After first-run gate, `[path]`, `--stack`, `--language`, `--name`, `--force`, Stack options -> unresolved target and parsed inputs (`InitCommand.cs:37-111`). | Current code creates the directory before validating (`:134`); proposed path must not do that. On first-run setup, rerun against the newly installed workloads. |
| Classify / CLI + project resolver | Target markers and config -> empty, adopt, heal, already initialized, or invalid/unsafe state (`InitCommand.cs:143-183`, `:459-473`). | Preserve adoption and language healing **without** engine creation or scaffolding. A complete project without force is refused. Diagnose readable malformed config without force; explicit force may regenerate it after validation. Unreadable/unsafe files remain errors, not blanket force permission. |
| Stack selection / existing initializers | Installed `IProjectInitializer` and contributed options -> chosen Stack/language, name, validated framework/bundle inputs (`InitCommand.cs:188-283`, `DotNetProjectInitializer.cs:57-85`). | Select/prompt or fail non-interactively; validate all required Stack options **before** cleanup. Keep the six existing initializer implementations working until each project's content is approved and qualified. |
| Project template selection / CLI + `Templater` | Only for a migrated creation route: captured context -> installed project entries -> one qualified default for Stack/language, exact variant. | Fresh target need not be an existing `FunctionsProject`. No production project-package registration is wired. Missing/ambiguous/incompatible content fails that route before mutation; adoption/heal bypass it. Do not silently switch to a different content source. |
| Bind/render / CLI + Stack + handle | Name, parsed Stack options, template parameters -> validated canonical values -> private planned files/directories and required configuration inputs. | Map host-owned options such as .NET `--target-framework` to authored parameters deliberately; do not reparse or make engine own Stack semantics. Preserve generated project behavior and setup per Stack. |
| Force/preflight / CLI | Rendered output, config and target state -> precise authorized effects. | Current `--force` clears content at `InitCommand.cs:287-295` before .NET's later framework validation and a `.git` **file** is not protected by `DirectoryGuard.ClearExceptGit`. Validate before any deletion; preserve Git metadata, verify paths/originals, and retain the current prompt/no-input authorization policy unless explicitly changed. |
| Publish/config / CLI + Stack | Approved effects -> generated files, then **required** `.func\config.json` with the selected Stack and language only where needed; setup steps only when prerequisites exist. | Current `WriteCliConfigurationFile` can warn and return success on persistence failure (`InitCommand.cs:576-630`). Proposed failure is nonzero with already-made effects and recovery guidance, not a fictional rollback. Adoption/heal merge existing config and preserve unrelated keys. |
| Exit/handoff / CLI | Valid project/config -> `func new [path]` resolves the same project context and selects an item; report command status and dispose any templater. | The `func new` path must see actual installed content and use its own command session. A partial init does not count as a successful handoff. No auto-run of `func new`, no cross-command process cache, and no loss of current Quickstart/runtime behavior. |

## 6. Distribution and hive boundary

The retained factory points to the `templates` directory under CLI home for Microsoft.TemplateEngine settings and installed packages. `WorkloadDeploymentService` installs workload payloads and registry metadata (`src\Func\Workloads\Install\WorkloadDeploymentService.cs:80-143`); the inspected production source does **not** register their template content with that engine hive. The separate .NET `dotnet new` hive does not satisfy this precondition.

**Before discovery:** approved content must be installed, registered in the correct hive, and attributable to its source/package identity and version where defined (test folder packages have no version). Release content needs an integrity reference. The engine reads template kind, identity, group/aliases, parameter/host metadata and supported constraints. Source/channel choice, where applicable, precedes ID matching. Without usable content, fail with actionable setup/content guidance and no target mutation; do not pretend an empty catalog means installation succeeded or install implicitly during invocation.

**Ownership proposal:** workload/content delivery and registration belong outside `Templater` (installer/setup and producer boundary); `Templater` consumes installed metadata and checks identity/compatibility, not feeds or producer repository layout. Sarah and Fabio must confirm who supplies the install-to-hive step and the exact package/version/channel contract. Tests can install local fixtures into an isolated hive as they already do, but the existing basic item fixture emits a text file and does not prove a generated function or parameter substitution (`test\Func.Tests\Templates\TemplateFixtures.cs:31-48`). The first command proof needs an approved, parameterized representative function template. Test registration is **not** production registration or a release package. Package integrity and actual installed-build behavior remain qualification gates.

## 7. Selection and parameter contracts

Keep three identities distinct: a concrete installed template (`TemplateCatalogEntry.Identity` plus scoped source/package version as needed), an explicit family (`GroupIdentity`), and a user reference (`--template` ID/alias). `TemplateType.Item`/`.Project` routes commands. Treat a missing group identity as a proposed singleton, never merge equal display names. Resolve within the selected source/kind/Stack/language context; detect duplicate applicable IDs or ambiguous aliases rather than taking the first package/mount-point match. The existing projector's first-package-per-mount-point behavior is adequate for listing but not an invocation tie-breaker (`TemplateCatalogProjector.cs:53-59`). Where historical channel selection permits a warned stable fallback, decide it **before** ID matching; do not change source after an explicit template rejection. Confirm source precedence and group fallback against real metadata.

`ListAsync` currently includes hidden entries and unusable host metadata for inspection (`Templater.cs:21-31`); the CLI must not imply these are runnable. Evaluate engine/package compatibility separately from project applicability, parameter validity and filesystem permission. Use supported Microsoft.TemplateEngine constraints plus the retained func workload/bundle declaration helpers once actually wired; capture installed workload and **resolved** bundle inputs, not a claimed version range or invented project capabilities. Unknown required input or unevaluated constraint is not proof of eligibility. Preserve diagnostics on zero candidates; select an existing `ResolvedTemplate` in the group and invoke through its issuing session.

`TemplateParameterDefinition` is the canonical command-facing parameter schema (`TemplateParameterProjector.cs:22-81`). The CLI parses template tokens **per eligible candidate**, keeps explicit values (even when equal to defaults), and intentionally maps host-owned options to canonical template symbols; unrelated aliases cannot shadow built-ins. Resolve authored versus evaluated defaults without erasing their origin. `--name` is command-owned and the projector excludes the engine's `name` symbol; the integration still validates its final canonical value. An eligible candidate can have missing required inputs; prompt after selection if interactive, otherwise fail with usable syntax. An invalid explicit input is an error, never silently replaced by a default.

## 8. Project context and lifetime

`IFunctionsProjectResolver` already identifies a project at a requested directory; `FunctionsProject` exposes `WorkingDirectory`, `StackName`, `Language` and worker/bundle support (`src\Abstractions\Projects\FunctionsProject.cs:10-27`). It **does not expose a capabilities collection or evaluated .NET framework**. Stack integration, not the shared engine, must capture any additionally required project-derived values once and bind them into validated canonical parameters. An init of a fresh project has no existing `FunctionsProject`; its chosen initializer and parsed options provide the context. No `ProjectFacts` duplicate or recapture/fingerprint framework is recommended.

`TemplateEngineContext` supplies the stable command/root/stack/language/bundle host values, and `ITemplaterFactory.Create` supplies a new synchronous-disposal session. That session owns discovery, the selected engine template and invocation; catalog-selection entries must be recognized as issued by it. Keep a single operation-local view, not a new process-global cache; engine-managed settings/cache can remain its implementation detail. On cancellation, failure or success, the command disposes it; failed initialization releases only resources actually acquired. Candidate invocation after disposal or with a foreign/stale entry fails explicitly. If a render uses a private output directory, its cleanup must be owned and its errors reported where material: the existing `TempDirectory.Dispose` currently swallows cleanup errors (`src\Func\Common\TempDirectory.cs:5-30`).

## 9. Filesystem safety and result semantics

**No target effects before validated selection, parameters and required Stack inputs.** Render to a private, bounded workspace; capture relative file bytes, explicit empty directories and any Stack-composed edits. If the underlying engine cannot render privately, the adapter must make that possible before enabling the command. Do not claim that existing `Templater.ListAsync` or `IFileSystem.WriteAllTextAsync` supplies this guarantee.

CLI-owned preflight validates destination and protected ancestors, path traversal/aliasing, required originals, collisions, config effects, force cleanup and cancellation **before** any target mutation. A small CLI-side publish helper may reuse `IFileSystem.MoveFile(overwrite: false)` for a create; it still needs guarded replace/modify and OS-specific race qualification. `DirectoryGuard.ClearExceptGit` is **not** safe as-is for a Git worktree pointer file. No public publisher interface, generic transaction engine or promise of all-or-nothing publication is justified.

`TemplateInvocationResult` describes the private render's planned effects; CLI publication records **actual** created/modified/preserved/deleted and, on interruption, pending or uncertain effects. For `func init`, required configuration is finalized after project files; a persistence failure is a command failure even if generation succeeded. For `func new`, preserve unrelated project files; later Python append and .NET project edits need stack-owned composition, complete-result validation and guarded originals before publication. Force does not bypass eligibility, unsafe targets or changed inputs. Cancellation is checked before mutation and between effects; cleanup, external Stack setup and partial writes receive explicit diagnostics, not success-shaped fallbacks.

The two linked research reports there are absent here; do not infer passing runtime behavior from those citations.

| Behavior / evidence | Proposed disposition and rationale | Required qualification or decision |

| Template IDs, aliases, groups (`R12`, `R14`) | **PRESERVE** established public IDs and case behavior where supported; **OPEN DECISION** on new alias/family fallback and hidden explicit-ID access. | Fixture for same-name variants, scoped duplicate IDs, ambiguous aliases and selected-entry identity through invocation. |
| Parameters, defaults and explicit input (`R15-R17`, `BC02`, `BC04`) | **PRESERVE** documented effective aliases; **SUPERSEDE** silently ignored invalid input, subject to team approval. Keep required prompting a proposal, not historical fact. | Compare actual package declarations with generated values; test aliases, default origin, conflicts, noninteractive and missing/invalid inputs. |
| Compatibility and constraints (`R13`, `BC03`, `BC07`) | **PRESERVE** applicable stack and bundle gates; **OPEN DECISION** on profile/no-bundle HTTP policy and unknown evidence. No unregistered constraint counts as passed. | Installed workload/bundle fixture, supported engine constraints, required unknowns, list versus create and stable fallback. |
| Prompting and selection (`R14`, `R17`) | **PRESERVE** interactive selection and explicit noninteractive intent; **OPEN DECISION** on precedence when several eligible variants remain. | Interactive/cancel/no-input, single explicit choice, zero candidates with diagnostics, and ambiguity without arbitrary order. |
| Generated content and project/item integration (`R02`, `R20-R24`) | **PRESERVE** current `func init` adoption/heal and working initializers; **OPEN DECISION** on migration/content inventory. Do not equate two proof templates with release parity. | Six Stack project paths, Node JS/TS, .NET C#/F#, Python; qualify Python app composition, .NET project/source integration, explicit directories and actual Host discovery. | Collisions and force (`R25`, `BC01`, `BC06`, F3) | **PRESERVE** explicit force authorization; **SUPERSEDE** destructive-before-validation and false partial success on approval. | Cancellation, errors and finalization (`R23-R25`, F4) | **SUPERSEDE** required configuration failures reported as success; retain actionable errors and honest partial effects, not automatic rollback. | Config failure after generation, abort before/after writes, setup warnings versus required failure and private cleanup error. |

No hidden acquisition on render. | Local fixture, installed packages across OS/RID, missing/corrupt content, version/channel selection and offline availability separate from dependency setup. |

## 11. Phase 3 findings F1-F6

| Finding | Design disposition / later work |
|---|---|
| F1 - Superseded architecture | Fabio's model leads; the Working Design supplies historical behavior, not extraction or replacement requirements. Physical extraction remains post-GA. |
| F2 - Grammar | Current `--format` remains; historical `--output` is not silently reinstated. Parser coverage is an implementation gate. |
| F3 - Destructive ordering | **Existing defect:** `func init --force` clears before some .NET framework validation. Require validated inputs and private output before cleanup; fix and qualify in an authorized implementation transaction. |
| F4 - Finalization failure | **Existing defect:** CLI config persistence can warn yet succeed. Treat required finalization failure as command failure with actual generated effects. |
| F5 - First-run | **Inherited behavior/qualification gap:** setup may return success before `func new`; distinguish preemption from creation failure and qualify cold starts. |
| F6 - Missing research | Historical research links are unavailable in this checkout. Cite only the committed summaries for historical claims; request exact artifacts before artifact-specific parity decisions. |

## 12. Terminology compliance

This proposal introduces no prohibited legacy naming in APIs, diagrams, prose or work items; it does not rename historical source identifiers or third-party contracts. **Runtime** means Azure Functions Host/app runtime; **Stack** means language stack; **Generic Template** refers to the Templating Engine concept. Use *shared CLI Templates layer* for cross-Stack orchestration and *project compatibility matcher* when an explicit matcher is needed. A CLI template host parameter is not an Azure Functions Host setting.

## 13. Open decisions for Fabio, Sarah and Francisco

The recommendations in section 4 are review inputs, not approvals. Resolve the token/constraint seam, private render/publication safety and registration first; the other API and ownership decisions follow. Absence of a release package or a platform safety proof blocks **implementation/qualification claims**, not Principal review of this proposal.

| Decision / owner to confirm | Evidence and recommended option | Alternative and consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Essential types - Fabio | Keep existing factory/context/catalog/parameter/session; add only simple group, exact handle and request/result values. | Drop `TemplateGroup` only if a real multi-variant fixture can preserve family diagnostics and narrowing without it; do not invent a candidate graph. |
| Group/candidate selection - Fabio + Francisco | Explicit family identity; singleton fallback; selection stays pinned to the same entry/session. | Display-name grouping or new lookup can select the wrong variant; precedence ties need explicit policy or ambiguity error. |
| `TemplateKind` versus `TemplateType` - Fabio | Use existing `TemplateType` for project/item. | A second enum requires mapping with no proven need; use it only if a concrete contract boundary demands different semantics. |
| Workload-to-hive registration - Sarah + Fabio | Installer/setup supplies validated local packages and registers them before discovery; templater stays read-only. | On-demand install inside discovery couples command UX to network/state and can leave an inconsistent catalog; release package format/channel is still open. |
| Factory/session lifetime - Fabio | Keep sync `Create`/`IDisposable` and one command-scoped snapshot; add async cleanup only when a required resource proves it necessary. | Process cache plus fresh sessions increases state/lifetime surfaces without a demonstrated caller. |
| Invocation/result/effects - Fabio + Francisco | Private render with typed **planned** effects; CLI guards/publishes and reports actual writes/config status. | Direct target generation cannot guarantee validation-before-destruction; platform-safe replace, output lifetime and cleanup need evidence. |
| Representative proof versus GA inventory - Fabio + Sarah + Francisco | Start with one item, then one project; agree on per-Stack content/negative cases before release gate. | Claiming parity from two templates ignores historic Node/Python/.NET item coverage and the draft's broader target. |
| Scaffolding ownership - Fabio (confirm with Francisco) | Agree on contract boundaries before assigning the first API increment. | Parallel uncoordinated scaffolding risks incompatible entry points. No lane allocated here. |
| Content migration ownership - Sarah (confirm with Francisco) | Agree on template package versions, metadata, fixtures and producer/consumer handoff. | Unavailable or unauthenticated payloads cannot certify actual IDs, parameters or effects. |
| Command parser and constraint seam - Fabio + CLI owner | Choose a bounded way for template tokens to reach candidate-specific validation; register/evaluate required func constraints using captured context. | Eager unknown-option rejection or `NotEvaluated` treated as eligible would make the proposed flow impossible or unsound. |

## 14. Minimum implementation increment after approval

1. Keep the existing supported `func init` initializers and `func new` unavailability guard until a qualified item path exists. Reuse the current internal factory, session and catalog; implement scoped resolution, immutable group narrowing and an exact candidate handle with disposal checks. No new public assembly, package manager or global cache.
2. Obtain an approved, parameterized item template that generates a real function for a chosen supported Stack; install it in an isolated test hive, then prove its parameter reaches the output through the real `func new` command with private invocation and guarded, CLI-owned publication. A metadata-only text-file fixture is a prerequisite test, **not** this acceptance journey. Preserve `--format`, noninteractive errors, first-run behavior, existing files and the no-write failure guarantee. Unsupported/unavailable routes remain explicit failures, not fabricated success.
3. Then qualify one project template through `func init`, including required config, a valid `func new` item in the generated project, and the F3/F4 safety fixes. Migrate each existing Stack initializer only after content, options, generated files and setup behavior are qualified; no silent feature retirement or new lane allocation here.

Approval dependencies: resolved token-parsing seam, package registration for real installs, supported constraints, private output, platform-safe publication and agreed content ownership. An empty `--list` or test-only folder registration is not proof of production readiness.

## 15. Tests and qualification (planned, not run)

Extend existing `TemplaterTests`, factory/session and metadata/constraint assertions; add candidate identity across list/resolve/invoke, same-family variants, malformed metadata, no content, cancellation, disposal and foreign-entry rejection. Add parser and command tests for built-in `--format`, template-specific aliases, explicit-default provenance, missing/invalid input and first-run short-circuit. For actual outputs, test parameter substitution, safe path/collision/force preflight, empty directories, required configuration failure and precise partial effects. Cover Stack-owned Python append and .NET source/project changes only with approved representative packages and concrete fixtures.

Separately authorized qualification must exercise `init -> new -> Host discovery` for approved Stack/language cases, adoption/healing and first-run, installed package integrity/channel selection, unsafe paths, cancellation, OS-specific replace semantics, installed RID payloads, and distinctions between template availability and dependency setup. Existing tests are **assertions, not executed results in this transaction**. **RUNTIME VALIDATION REQUIRED.**

## 16. Principal review handoff

Review this one uncommitted proposal against the four committed documents at the pinned candidate. Priority challenges: (1) can the engine render privately and retain exact entry/package identity; (2) do token parsing and required constraints reach the command path without duplicate catalogs; (3) is the smallest family/candidate model sufficient; (4) can validation, force and required CLI finalization avoid false success while reporting partial effects; (5) are workload registration and per-Stack release coverage clearly separated from the first proof? F1-F6 and all historical rows above have explicit proposals or named open decisions, not implementation approval. Phase 5 has **not** begun.
